records.source: טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו וְה֣וּא כְסִֽיל׃
records.gloss: Better [is the] poor walking in his integrity than [one] perverse [in] his lips, and he [is] a fool.
pieces: Better to be poor and live with integrity \q than to be a fool with a lying tongue.

L.1: Better [is the] poor who walks in {{gender:their|his}} integrity \q than one crooked in {{gender:their|his}} speech who [is] a fool.

R.1: It is better to be poor and honest than to be a foolish liar.

decisions.choice: better poor with integrity: as in 28:6
decisions.reason: 28:6 has "than one crooked in his ways who is rich"; here the contrast is with a fool.

records.source: גַּ֤ם בְּלֹא־דַ֣עַת נֶ֣פֶשׁ לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְאָ֖ץ בְּרַגְלַ֣יִם חוֹטֵֽא׃
records.gloss: Also without knowledge desire [is] not good, and [one] hastening with feet misses.
pieces: Zeal without knowledge is not good; \q whoever rushes ahead misses the way.

L.2: Also, desire without knowledge [is] not good, \q and one who hurries with [the] feet misses [the way].

R.2: Being eager is not good if you do not know what you are doing. \q If you rush, you will make mistakes.

decisions.choice: desire: eagerness, zeal (nephesh)
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) is appetite or desire (16:26); some read "a person without knowledge".

decisions.choice: misses: misses the mark, sins
decisions.reason: The verb (hata) of 8:36.

records.source: אִוֶּ֣לֶת אָ֭דָם תְּסַלֵּ֣ף דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְעַל־יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִזְעַ֥ף לִבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] folly of a person subverts his way, and against YHWH his heart rages.
pieces: People ruin their lives by their own folly, \q and then their hearts rage against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: A person's folly ruins {{gender:their|his}} way, \q and {{gender:their|his}} heart rages against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: People ruin their own lives by being foolish. \q Then they get angry at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: rages against the LORD: blaming God
decisions.reason: Fools blame God for the results of their own folly (compare Genesis 3:12).

records.source: ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּיִפָּרֵֽד׃
records.gloss: Wealth adds many friends, but a poor [person] from his friend is separated.
pieces: Wealth brings many friends, \q but the poor lose even the friends they have.

L.4: Wealth adds many friends, \q but [the] poor is separated from {{gender:their|his}} friend.

R.4: Rich people have many friends. \q But poor people lose the friends they have.

decisions.choice: an observation, as in 14:20
decisions.reason: See 14:20 and verse 7.

records.source: עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט׃
records.gloss: A witness of lies will not go unpunished, and [one] breathing out lies will not escape.
pieces: A false witness will not escape punishment, \q and one who pours out lies will not get away.

L.5: A false witness will not go unpunished, \q and one who breathes out lies will not escape.

R.5: A witness who lies in court will be punished. \q People who tell lies will not escape.

decisions.choice: a false witness: punished by law
decisions.reason: The law gave the false witness the punishment meant for the accused (Deuteronomy 19:16–19). Verse 9 repeats the saying.

records.source: רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי־נָדִ֑יב וְכָל־הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן׃
records.gloss: Many entreat [the] face of a noble, and everyone [is a] friend to a man of gifts.
pieces: Many try to win a ruler's favor, \q and everyone is a friend to the one who gives gifts.

L.6: Many seek [the] favor of a noble, \q and everyone [is a] friend to one who gives gifts.

R.6: Many people try to please important people. \q Everyone wants to be friends with someone who gives presents.

decisions.choice: entreat the face: seek favor
decisions.reason: Compare 29:26.

records.source: כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי־רָ֨שׁ׀שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לוֹ־הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: All [the] brothers of [the] poor hate him; how much more his friends are far from him! [He is] pursuing words; to him they [are].
pieces: All the relatives of the poor shun them; \q how much more do their friends keep away! \q The poor go after them with pleas, but they are gone.

L.7: All [the] brothers of [the] poor hate {{gender:them|him}}; \q how much more do {{gender:their|his}} friends keep far from {{gender:them|him}}! \q {{gender:They pursue|He pursues}} [them with] words, [but] they [are gone].

R.7: Poor people are avoided even by their families. \q Their friends stay away even more. \q When they beg for help, no one is there.

decisions.choice: the third line: he pursues them with words, but they are gone
alternatives: a different full line (the ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: This is the only three-line saying in the collection, and the last line is obscure. The written consonants (ketiv) read "they are not"; the scribes' reading (qere) "to him they are". The ancient Greek has two extra lines. The sense seems to be that the poor man's pleading finds no one.

records.source: קֹֽנֶה־לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: [One] acquiring heart loves his self; [one] keeping understanding [is] to find good.
pieces: To gain sense is to love yourself; \q to hold on to understanding is to prosper.

L.8: Whoever gets heart loves {{gender:their|his}} own self; \q whoever keeps understanding will find good.

R.8: If you become wise, you are doing yourself a favor. \q If you keep on understanding, good things will happen to you.

decisions.choice: gets heart: gains sense

records.source: עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֖יחַ כְּזָבִ֣ים יֹאבֵֽד׃פ
records.gloss: A witness of lies will not go unpunished, and [one] breathing out lies will perish.
pieces: A false witness will not escape punishment, \q and one who pours out lies will perish.

L.9: A false witness will not go unpunished, \q and one who breathes out lies will perish.

R.9: A witness who lies in court will be punished. \q People who tell lies will die.

decisions.choice: repeats verse 5, with "will perish"
decisions.reason: See verse 5.

records.source: לֹֽא־נָאוֶ֣ה לִכְסִ֣יל תַּעֲנ֑וּג אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־לְעֶ֤בֶד׀מְשֹׁ֬ל בְּשָׂרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Not fitting for a fool [is] luxury; how much less for a slave to rule over princes!
pieces: Luxury does not suit a fool; \q still less should a servant rule over princes.

L.10: Luxury [is] not fitting for a fool; \q how much less for a slave to rule over princes!

R.10: It is wrong for a fool to live in luxury. \q It is even worse for a servant to rule over princes.

decisions.choice: a slave ruling princes: the world upside down
decisions.reason: A common picture of social disorder (30:22; Ecclesiastes 10:7). 17:2 shows a wise servant may rightly rise.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The meaning decision (m1) keeps the picture of the lowest ruling the highest.

records.source: שֵׂ֣כֶל אָ֭דָם הֶאֱרִ֣יךְ אַפּ֑וֹ וְ֝תִפאַרְתּ֗וֹעֲבֹ֣ר עַל־פָּֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: [The] prudence of a person makes long his anger, and his glory [is] to pass over a transgression.
pieces: Good sense makes a person patient, \q and it is to their credit to overlook an offense.

L.11: A person's good sense makes {{gender:them|him}} slow to anger, \q and it is {{gender:their|his}} glory to overlook an offense.

R.11: Wise people do not get angry quickly. \q It is good to forgive people when they wrong you.

decisions.choice: pass over an offense: forgive, let it go
decisions.reason: Compare 10:12 and 17:9.

records.source: נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל־עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A roar like a lion [is the] rage of a king, but like dew on grass [is] his favor.
pieces: A king in a rage roars like a lion, \q but his goodwill falls like dew on the grass.

L.12: A king's rage [is] like [the] roar of a lion, \q but his favor [is] like dew on [the] grass.

R.12: An angry king is as scary as a roaring lion. \q But when he is pleased, he is like refreshing dew on the grass.

decisions.choice: lion ... dew: as in 16:14–15 and 20:2

records.source: הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: Ruin to his father [is] a foolish son, and a continual dripping [are the] quarrels of a wife.
pieces: A foolish son ruins his father, \q and a quarrelsome wife is like a leaky roof that never stops dripping.

L.13: A foolish son [is] ruin to his father, \q and [the] quarrels of a wife [are] a constant dripping.

R.13: A foolish son can ruin his father. \q A wife who is always arguing is as annoying as a roof that always leaks.

decisions.choice: a constant dripping: a leaking roof
decisions.reason: The picture recurs in 27:15. Flat roofs leaked in the rainy season.

records.source: בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: House and wealth [are] an inheritance of fathers, but from YHWH [is] a prudent wife.
pieces: House and wealth are inherited from parents, \q but a sensible wife is from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: House and wealth [are] an inheritance from {{gender:parents|fathers}}, \q but a prudent wife [is] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: You can get a house and money from your parents. \q But only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} can give you a wise wife.

decisions.choice: a prudent wife from the LORD: as in 18:22

records.source: עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב׃
records.gloss: Laziness casts into deep sleep, and a slack person will hunger.
pieces: Laziness brings on deep sleep, \q and an idle person will go hungry.

L.15: Laziness casts [one] into deep sleep, \q and an idle person will go hungry.

R.15: Lazy people sleep too much. \q People who do not work will go hungry.

decisions.choice: deep sleep: heavy, senseless sleep
decisions.reason: The word (tardemah) of Genesis 2:21.

records.source: שֹׁמֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ בּוֹזֵ֖ה דְרָכָ֣יו יָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: [One] keeping a commandment keeps his life; [one] despising his ways will die.
pieces: Whoever keeps the commandment preserves their life, \q but whoever is careless about how they live will die.

L.16: Whoever keeps [the] commandment keeps {{gender:their|his}} life; \q whoever despises {{gender:their|his}} ways will die.

R.16: If you obey God's commands, you will live. \q If you do not care how you live, you will die.

decisions.choice: will die, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: will be put to death (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "will be put to death"; the scribes' reading (qere) "will die".

decisions.choice: despises his ways: is careless how he lives
decisions.reason: "His ways" may be the person's own conduct or God's ways.

decisions.choice: God's commands
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who commands, which the verse implies.

records.source: מַלְוֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה ח֣וֹנֵֽן דָּ֑ל וּ֝גְמֻל֗וֹ יְשַׁלֶּם־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [One] lending [to] YHWH [is one] showing favor [to the] poor, and his deed he will repay to him.
pieces: Whoever is kind to the poor is lending to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pay them back for what they have done.

L.17: Whoever is kind to [the] poor lends to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay {{gender:them|him}} for {{gender:their|his}} deed.

R.17: When you help poor people, it is like lending money to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q He will pay you back.

decisions.choice: lending to the LORD
decisions.reason: God takes the side of the poor so fully that kindness to them is a loan to him (14:31; Matthew 25:40).

records.source: יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְאֶל־הֲ֝מִית֗וֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: Discipline your son, for there is hope, and to killing him do not lift your soul.
pieces: Discipline your son while there is still hope; \q do not make yourself responsible for his death.

L.18: Discipline your son while there is hope, \q and do not set your heart on his death.

R.18: Correct your son while he is young enough to learn. \q If you do not, you may help lead him to death.

decisions.choice: do not set your heart on his death
alternatives: do not be so angry that you kill him
do not let him go to death by neglecting discipline
decisions.reason: The line is hard. It may warn against punishing in rage, or against neglecting discipline and so letting the son go to ruin (23:13–14). Either way, discipline is for his life, not his harm.

records.source: גְּֽדָל־חֵ֭מָה נֹ֣שֵׂא עֹ֑נֶשׁ כִּ֥י אִם־תַּ֝צִּ֗יל וְע֣וֹד תּוֹסִֽף׃
records.gloss: A great [one] of rage bears a fine, for if you rescue, also again you will add.
pieces: A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty; \q if you bail them out, you will only have to do it again.

L.19: A person of great anger must pay [the] penalty; \q for if you rescue [them], you will have to do it again.

R.19: Let people with bad tempers face the results. \q If you rescue them, you will have to do it again and again.

decisions.choice: great of anger, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) give an unclear word; the scribes' reading (qere) is "great".

records.source: שְׁמַ֣ע עֵ֭צָה וְקַבֵּ֣ל מוּסָ֑ר לְ֝מַ֗עַן תֶּחְכַּ֥ם בְּאַחֲרִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, so that you may be wise in your end.
pieces: Listen to advice and accept correction, \q so that in the end you will be wise.

L.20: Listen to advice and accept discipline, \q so that you may be wise in your latter days.

R.20: Listen to advice and accept correction. \q Then you will become wise.

decisions.choice: in your end: later in life
decisions.reason: Or "from now on".

records.source: רַבּ֣וֹת מַחֲשָׁב֣וֹת בְּלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וַעֲצַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: Many plans [are] in [the] heart of a person, but [the] purpose of YHWH, it will stand.
pieces: People have many plans in their minds, \q but it is the purpose of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that will prevail.

L.21: Many plans [are] in a person's heart, \q but [the] purpose of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will stand.

R.21: People make lots of plans. \q But only what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wants will happen.

decisions.choice: plans ... purpose: as in 16:1, 9

records.source: תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְטֽוֹב־רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב׃
records.gloss: [The] desire of a person [is] his loyalty, and better [is the] poor than a man of lies.
pieces: What people want in a person is loyalty; \q better to be poor than a liar.

L.22: What is desired in a person [is] {{gender:their|his}} loyal love, \q and [the] poor [is] better than a liar.

R.22: People want friends who are loyal. \q It is better to be poor than to be a liar.

decisions.choice: what is desired in a person is loyal love
alternatives: a person's desire is his shame (hesed as in 14:34)
a person's greed is his disgrace
decisions.reason: The first line can be read several ways, since hesed can also mean "shame" (14:34).

records.source: יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה לְחַיִּ֑ים וְשָׂבֵ֥עַ יָ֝לִ֗ין בַּל־יִפָּ֥קֶד רָֽע׃
records.gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [leads] to life, and satisfied he will rest; he will not be visited [by] harm.
pieces: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} leads to life; \q whoever has it rests content, untouched by trouble.

L.23: [The] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [leads] to life; \q one rests satisfied, untouched by harm.

R.23: Honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe leads to life. \q People who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} sleep well and are safe from harm.

decisions.choice: rests: spends the night
decisions.reason: The verb (lin) of 15:31.

records.source: טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת גַּם־אֶל־פִּ֝֗יהוּ לֹ֣א יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; even to his mouth he does not bring it back.
pieces: The lazy bury their hand in the dish \q and will not even lift it back to their mouth.

L.24: [The] sluggard buries {{gender:their|his}} hand in the dish; \q {{gender:they do|he does}} not even bring it back to {{gender:their|his}} mouth.

R.24: Some people are so lazy that they put their hand in the food bowl \q but do not even lift the food to their mouths.

decisions.choice: buries his hand in the dish: a humorous picture
decisions.reason: People ate from a common dish with their hands. The saying returns in 26:15.

records.source: לֵ֣ץ תַּ֭כֶּה וּפֶ֣תִי יַעְרִ֑ם וְהוֹכִ֥יחַ לְ֝נָב֗וֹן יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃
records.gloss: A mocker you strike, and [the] simple will become prudent; and reprove [one] understanding, he will understand knowledge.
pieces: Flog a mocker, and the naive will learn a lesson; \q correct the discerning, and they will gain knowledge.

L.25: Strike a mocker, and [the] simple will become prudent; \q reprove [one who] understands, and {{gender:they|he}} will understand knowledge.

R.25: When a mocker is punished, foolish people learn a lesson. \q When wise people are corrected, they learn even more.

decisions.choice: the mocker is not changed, but others learn
decisions.reason: The mocker himself will not learn (9:7–8), but the simple watching him will (21:11).

records.source: מְֽשַׁדֶּד־אָ֭ב יַבְרִ֣יחַ אֵ֑ם בֵּ֝֗ן מֵבִ֥ישׁ וּמַחְפִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: [One] assaulting a father, [who] drives away a mother, [is] a son bringing shame and disgrace.
pieces: A son who robs his father and drives out his mother \q brings shame and disgrace.

L.26: One who robs [his] father [and] drives away [his] mother \q [is] a son who brings shame and disgrace.

R.26: A son who steals from his father and forces his mother out of her home \q brings shame on himself.

decisions.choice: dishonoring parents: against the fifth commandment
decisions.reason: The law set a heavy penalty on cursing or striking parents (Exodus 21:15, 17; Proverbs 20:20; 28:24).

records.source: חַֽדַל־בְּ֭נִילִשְׁמֹ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר לִ֝שְׁג֗וֹת מֵֽאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Cease, my son, to listen to discipline, to stray from words of knowledge.
pieces: My son, if you stop listening to correction, \q you will stray from the words of knowledge.

L.27: Stop, my son, listening to discipline \q [only] to stray from words of knowledge.

R.27: My son, if you stop listening when you are corrected, \q you will forget what you have learned.

decisions.choice: cease ... to stray: an ironic command
alternatives: Cease listening to instruction that leads you astray
decisions.reason: Read as irony: "Go ahead, stop listening, and you will wander off." Or: stop listening to teaching that leads astray.

records.source: עֵ֣ד בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָלִ֣יץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְבַלַּע־אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: A witness of worthlessness mocks justice, and [the] mouth of wicked [people] swallows wickedness.
pieces: A corrupt witness makes a mockery of justice, \q and the wicked swallow evil whole.

L.28: A worthless witness mocks justice, \q and [the] mouth of [the] wicked gulps down wickedness.

R.28: A dishonest witness makes fun of justice. \q Evil people love evil the way hungry people love food.

decisions.choice: swallows wickedness: devours it eagerly
decisions.reason: Compare Job 15:16.

records.source: נָכ֣וֹנוּ לַלֵּצִ֣ים שְׁפָטִ֑ים וּ֝מַהֲלֻמ֗וֹת לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃
records.gloss: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for [the] back of fools.
pieces: Penalties stand ready for mockers, \q and the rod for fools' backs.

L.29: Punishments are prepared for mockers, \q and beatings for [the] backs of fools.

R.29: Mockers will be punished. \q Fools will be beaten.

decisions.choice: the rod for the back: as in 10:13
